# Calibration: what "good" looks like by level and target

Judge the resume against the **competition at this level**, not against a perfect resume.

| Level | Strong resume has | Acceptable | Roast-worthy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1st–2nd year student | 1–2 original projects, one deployed; learning in public (GitHub activity); a hackathon or club role | Course projects with clean READMEs | Empty GitHub; only certificates; a two-page resume |
| Pre-final year (internship hunt) | 2–3 projects with real users or a technical twist; DSA proof (a rating, or 200+ problems); an open-source PR or hackathon win | Solid projects, no DSA proof yet | Tutorial clones only; skills lists with 20 technologies |
| Final year / fresher | An internship (any), 2–3 strong deployed projects, DSA proof for product targets, impact metrics | Projects without metrics | No links; "Responsible for"; objective-statement clichés |
| 0–2 yrs experience | Work impact first (shipped features, metrics, scale); one standout project optional | Thin metrics | College projects above work experience; listing coursework |
| 2–5 yrs experience | Ownership, scale, cross-team impact, mentoring, system design signals | Feature lists | No progression; duties instead of outcomes |

## By target

| Target | What the screen weights most |
|---|---|
| Service / mass recruiters | CGPA and eligibility, clean format, core-subject basics, communication |
| Product companies | Projects with depth, internships, DSA proof, impact bullets |
| Big tech | Impact at scale, metrics, strong DSA signals, recognisable internships, clarity |
| Startups | Shipped things, breadth, ownership, GitHub and live demos, speed |
| International / remote | Concise English, impact-first, clear time zone or work authorisation, portfolio |

## By market

- **India campus**: one page, CGPA prominent if ≥ 7.5, a coding-platform rating is a strong signal, no photo needed.
- **US / UK / EU**: one page for new grads, no photo, no date of birth or marital status, impact-first.
- **Other markets**: follow local norms where they differ (some regions expect a photo). Ask if unsure.

Never invent salary bands, acceptance rates or market statistics. If you cite a market condition, it must come from the user, a cited source, or be clearly marked as a general observation.
